causal_identification_attacks: The key causal claim requires exact pool identity and acting invariance. Any difference in served winner, prompt serialization, verifier access, tool trace truncation, or updater token budget across arms confounds projection with evidence quality or budget.

Precommitted rollout-0 is not a clean substitute for a rejected witness if rollout-0 has different position bias, temperature realization, length, tool-use pattern, or verifier-score distribution from the counterfactual winner-conditioned evidence.

The rejected-witness rule must be frozen before outcomes. Choosing the most informative, hardest, or representative failure after seeing trajectories reintroduces outcome-dependent selection and can manufacture delta.

delta_z is not identifiable from observational success/failure feedback comparisons because mixed pools differ from all-success and all-fail pools in task difficulty and latent family prevalence. It needs cloned updater states and held-out probes.

The longitudinal reversal can be confounded by skill-state divergence after the first update: later high-K pools are no longer the same across arms. The paper must separate first-update causal effects from path-dependent evolution effects.

Held-out validation gating can itself preferentially accept patches from certain evidence types. Acceptance rate, patch type, and rejection memory must be reported or the gate becomes part of the treatment.

If frozen evaluation uses tasks related to the evolution tasks by workbook, template, or family leakage, the estimated future-skill gain may be instance memorization rather than reusable skill learning.

The scientific unit must remain complete independent evolution streams or cloned learned-skill states. Treating rollouts, patches, tasks, or repeated endpoint calls as independent n would invalidate uncertainty estimates.
review.decisive_kill_experiment: Run the cloned-state same-pool intervention on a qualified substrate: same initial skill hash, same task batch, same exact K-pool hashes, same served winner, same updater and update seed, and compare winner-only versus precommitted rejected-witness learning evidence, followed by common frozen K=1 held-out evaluation. If the rejected witness does not improve future frozen skill in the preregistered direction—especially in mixed rescue pools with positive estimated diagnostic value—the central mechanism is dead.

deeper_scientific_object.object: Decision-induced observation kernels for persistent learning from search: a deployed selector maps a generated search object to served behavior and separately determines the updater-visible evidence measure, thereby controlling the future learning distribution.
deeper_scientific_object.why_deeper: This object contains Search-Projection Censoring as a special case, connects selective labels, performative prediction, DAgger, and search distillation, and makes the real scientific variable the observation kernel rather than search budget, contrastive prompting, or failure feedback. It also explains both harmful and beneficial search regimes through what evidence is retained, not through compute amount.

review.formula_or_mechanism_that_is_pretty_but_: The mutual-information diagnostic-retention quantity D_g = I(Z; g(T_K) | x, S_t) is currently attractive but mostly decorative outside the controlled suite. In real benchmarks Z is not identified, the estimator is not specified, and data processing only gives a weak inequality that does not imply a fixed LLM updater benefits from richer evidence. The paper should not present this as a measured mechanism unless Z is operationally defined and the estimator is validated.
review.irreducible_novelty: The only currently defensible irreducible novelty is the coupled package: (1) an independence-free rescue-censoring identity linking acting gain to winner-only failure-visibility loss on the same search pool; (2) an exact-same-pool, fixed-acting-winner cloned intervention that changes only the learning projection; and (3) prospective prediction of held-out frozen-skill deficits from pre-outcome censoring mass times diagnostic value. The novelty is not CADP, contrastive packets, or failure usefulness.

method_collision_assessment.SkillCAT: Direct method collision. It already covers same-task success/failure contrast, divergence extraction, external skill editing, and replay validation. R17 survives only if the serving-selection censoring law, same-pool fixed-winner intervention, and prospective frozen-skill prediction remain central and SkillCAT is treated as a mandatory baseline.
method_collision_assessment.TopoCurate: Representation and selection collision. It already argues that outcome filtering discards useful branch structure and uses topology containing effective and failure branches for training-data selection. R17 must emphasize external persistent skill updating, winner-only serving-induced observation loss, and future frozen-skill endpoints rather than generic branch-structure value.
other: Rethinking Self-Evolving Agent Skills removes novelty from failure feedback being useful and from test-time scaling differing from persistent skill gains.
Search-E1, SGCD, OVCSD, and SKILL-KD remove novelty from sibling contrast, first divergence, and teacher/student trajectory patching.
SkillOpt removes novelty from bounded edits, held-out acceptance, and rejected-edit memory.
TSR, Expert Iteration, AlphaZero-style distillation, and best-of-N teacher selection falsify any universal claim that more search harms learning.

Selective labels, performative prediction, and DAgger supply the mature conceptual parent class; R17 must present itself as a new instance with a new measurement law, not as the discovery of decision-dependent data.

review.recommendation: REVISE_BEFORE_ANY_EXECUTION. Do not stop yet, but narrow the paper to the mechanism-level serving-induced observation-kernel claim; add SkillCAT and TopoCurate as mandatory baselines; make the identity independence-free; freeze the mixed-event intervention and disjoint family partition; replace the old R3 runner; and treat CADP as optional unless it beats the simpler Rejected-Witness arm under matched budgets.
review.single_sentence_verdict: R17 is not novel as contrastive failure-based skill editing, but it may still be novel as a causal and predictive study of how winner-only serving over a shared search pool censors an external persistent learner—provided the same-pool intervention and prospective Gamma-times-delta law survive SkillCAT-style controls.
review.strongest_direct_reduction: SkillCAT is the strongest direct reduction. It already combines same-task multi-rollout success/failure pairing, meaningful divergence extraction, skill-editable lesson generation, and replay validation in a persistent external skill pipeline. If R17's empirical effect is reproduced by a source-faithful SkillCAT-style contrast baseline without needing the serving-selection causal chain, then R17 becomes an application of SkillCAT plus a selective-labels interpretation rather than a new mechanism.
theory_attacks: The binary identity is exact only for the event {precommitted rollout fails, at least one other rollout succeeds}; it does not by itself establish learning harm. The paper must not slide from visibility loss to skill loss without independently estimating delta.

The i.i.d. Bernoulli curve and p*(K) are only a reference model. Correlated rollouts, shared prompts, shared latent mode, verifier quantization, and non-exchangeable rollout generation can move the empirical Gamma far from the analytic curve.

The continuous-verifier layer-cake identity is mathematically valid for max versus a fixed coordinate, but real selectors may use verifier ensembles, tie-breaking, constraints, or non-score rules; then the identity must be re-derived for the actual selector rather than assumed.

Gamma times delta is exact only if the alternative projection differs from winner-only exclusively inside the preregistered mixed rescue event. If CADP also changes all-fail or all-success handling, the factorization becomes an estimand of a bundled intervention, not the clean mechanism.

The family-level sum requires a mutually exclusive precommitted partition of mixed pools. Overlapping failure tags, post-hoc family assignment, or multiple deficiencies per trajectory will double-count pools and destroy calibration.

The intermediate-difficulty peak is a modeling assumption under the one-parameter i.i.d. specialization, not a theorem about natural task distributions. Difficulty mixture and family heterogeneity can flatten, shift, or eliminate the peak.

Data processing gives only I(Z; winner-only) <= I(Z; full pool). It does not imply greater value of information for a bounded LLM updater with finite context, attention failures, or validation-gated patch constraints.

The theory currently assumes the updater mapping U is stable enough that one-step cloned effects predict longitudinal evolution. Compounding edits, validation-gate drift, and skill-interference can break that bridge.

The broad phenomenon is already covered by selective labels, performative prediction, DAgger, search distillation, and failure-feedback skill evolution. The narrower residual—serving-time winner selection over a shared search pool causally censoring an external persistent skill updater, with an exact rescue-censoring law and same-pool intervention—has not been shown to be directly reduced by the supplied sources.
